title: Uncertainty in urban forest canopy assessment: Lessons from Seattle, WA, USA
relevance: The cautionary tale for this project, from 15 miles away and the same imagery ecosystem: assessed Seattle canopy cover varies substantially across studies for IDENTICAL dates, with multiple conflicting values published for 1972, 2002 and 2009. Methodological difference, not real canopy change, produced apparent trends that cities then acted on. This is the strongest available argument that our per-year numbers must ship with their method and uncertainty attached rather than as bare percentages, and it is regionally specific enough to cite directly in any Edmonds-facing write-up. Read it as the failure mode our honest-measurement workstream exists to avoid.

title: A comparison of two sampling approaches for assessing the urban forest canopy cover from aerial photography
relevance: Quantifies how much the ANSWER moves with the imagery source alone: canopy cover in Tallahassee estimated at 44.5-45.1% from NAIP versus 48.6-49.1% from Google Earth - roughly four percentage points from source choice, with no change on the ground. That is the same order as the disagreement between our own two references, and it establishes that source-driven variation of a few points is normal rather than a symptom of something broken in our pipeline. Also useful for setting the precision a point-sampling design must reach before a reported change is meaningful.
